messages.content:
The writer's note about it, in their words: 我想在 r/WarriorCats 发一个提问帖，问问大家的看法。
A learner of English is rewriting part of a post for Reddit question post:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he went really miserable and furious for that.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest skies, and it would be hard / not worth it to get back here for a distant little kittypet who wanted to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was an overcast day, so without the moonlight it makes sense they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books where the night sky was cloudy when some cat’s at the Moonstone? Or do StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t try again on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>
The part: "hard / not worth it"
What is wrong with it: Reader meets an open choice where the claim should be; 'hard' is about ability and effort, 'not worth it' about StarClan's choice, and these lead to different readings of Ravenpaw's account.
What they mean (confirmed by them): StarClan could not easily come back
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "too hard"
Words they already have as hints: difficult, effort, reach, tough
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in English, one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Name no English word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short English sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in English.
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"Choose one idea, because this part is about how difficult the return was, not whether StarClan wanted to come back. Use one describing word for that difficulty, then place a small word before it to show the level went beyond normal.","example":"Carrying all the boxes upstairs would be [too hard] for one person."}
